evals.description: Pending-reboot non-compliance; skill must recognize it's not a patch failure and needs a controlled reboot, gated on RebootIfNeeded/approval.
evals.prompt: An instance is NON_COMPLIANT with InstalledPendingRebootCount=3, but FailedCount=0 and MissingCount=0, and the Security Hub SSM.2 finding is open. The patch run used RebootOption=NoReboot. Do I need to re-run patching to fix this?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is not a patch failure — the patches installed successfully but the run used RebootOption=NoReboot, so reboot-requiring patches sit in InstalledPendingReboot and the instance reports non-compliant until it reboots. The fix is a single controlled reboot in an approved change window, not a re-patch. Cautions that because the run used NoReboot (a deliberate deferred-reboot policy), a reboot is a disruptive change requiring approval and application-owner sign-off, and cluster members must be rebooted one at a time. After the reboot, PendingReboot goes to 0 and Security Hub SSM.2 auto-resolves on its next evaluation.
assertions: States this is a pending-reboot state, not a patch failure, and does not require re-patching
Recommends a controlled reboot in an approved change window
Notes the NoReboot policy means a reboot needs approval (and cluster members one at a time)

evals.description: Shutdown-in-progress race; skill must recognize a timing race, use a bounded wait, and not loop-retry into a rebooting host.
evals.prompt: A Windows patch run failed immediately with 'Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation : A system shutdown is in progress.' and exit status 0xffffffff, before any patch was installed. This happened right after the previous patch cycle rebooted the instance. Should I just keep retrying the patch until it works?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is a reboot-timing/orchestration race, not a patch-content or connectivity failure — the patch started while the OS was still rebooting from the prior cycle, and Windows rejects new operations during shutdown. It is transient. The correct handling is a BOUNDED wait (poll PingStatus at most ~10 times / ~10 minutes) for the agent to come back Online, then confirm RebootPending=False and a fresh uptime before allowing a single retry (or letting the next scheduled cycle run). Warns explicitly against an indefinite retry loop and against retrying into a still-rebooting instance, and says if it never returns Online it is impaired — route to SSM connectivity triage rather than retrying.
assertions: Identifies a reboot-timing race rather than a patch or connectivity failure
Recommends a bounded wait for boot then a single retry, not an indefinite retry loop
Warns against retrying into a still-rebooting host and routes a never-Online instance to connectivity triage

evals.description: User wants to reboot to clear compliance; skill must gate on RebootIfNeeded vs NoReboot and approval before rebooting.
evals.prompt: Compliance shows pending reboot on a production instance and I want to just reboot it now to make the dashboard green. Anything I should check first?
evals.expected_output: Advises confirming it is purely reboot-pending first (FailedCount=0, MissingCount=0, InstalledPendingRebootCount>0) and that a reboot is actually pending in-guest. Critically, only reboot if the failed patch execution used RebootOption=RebootIfNeeded; if it used NoReboot, that reflects a deliberate deferred-reboot policy and rebooting is a disruptive change that needs an approved change window and application-owner confirmation — don't just reboot to green a dashboard. For clustered instances, reboot members one at a time to avoid quorum loss. After the approved reboot, compliance clears and Security Hub SSM.2 auto-resolves.
assertions: Says to verify it is purely reboot-pending before rebooting
Gates the reboot on RebootIfNeeded vs a deliberate NoReboot policy and on approval
Warns not to reboot a production instance just to green a dashboard without approval
